subject: bio
title: Cell Structure
subtitle: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells; organelle structure and function.
concept: Eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotic cells do not.
Organelle structure is directly linked to function — e.g. mitochondria have a folded inner membrane (cristae) to maximise ATP synthesis surface area.
Resolution and magnification are key microscopy concepts; electron microscopes give greater resolution than light microscopes.

notes.heading: Organelles — Structure and Function
items: Nucleus: contains chromatin (DNA + histone proteins); surrounded by nuclear envelope with pores; contains nucleolus (makes rRNA and assembles ribosomes).
Mitochondria: double membrane; inner membrane folded into cristae (site of ATP synthesis); matrix contains enzymes for Krebs cycle and DNA/ribosomes.
Chloroplast (plants): double membrane; thylakoid membranes (grana) for light-dependent reactions; stroma for light-independent (Calvin cycle).
Rough ER: has ribosomes on surface; site of protein synthesis and folding.
Smooth ER: no ribosomes; synthesises lipids and detoxifies substances.
Golgi apparatus: modifies and packages proteins into vesicles; produces lysosomes.
Lysosomes: contain hydrolytic enzymes; digest old organelles (autophagy) and foreign material.
Ribosomes: 80S (eukaryotes, free or on RER); 70S (prokaryotes, mitochondria, chloroplasts).
Cell wall (plants): cellulose microfibrils; provides strength and prevents lysis.
Vacuole (plants): filled with cell sap; maintains turgor.
Centrioles (animal cells): organise spindle fibres during cell division.

notes.heading: Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic
items: Prokaryotic: no nucleus; circular DNA; 70S ribosomes; no membrane-bound organelles; smaller (~1–10 μm).
Eukaryotic: true nucleus; linear DNA; 80S ribosomes; membrane-bound organelles; larger (~10–100 μm).
Prokaryotic features: cell wall (peptidoglycan in bacteria); plasmids; flagellum; capsule (some).

notes.heading: Microscopy
items: Resolution: minimum distance between two points that can be seen as distinct.
Light microscope: max resolution ~200 nm; can view living cells; uses visible light; cheaper.
Transmission EM: resolution ~0.1 nm; shows internal ultrastructure; dead/stained specimens only.
Scanning EM: shows surface structure in 3D.

definitions.body: A membrane-bound structure within a eukaryotic cell with a specific function.
The minimum distance between two points that can still be seen as separate points.
Image size divided by actual size: M = I/A.
Folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane that increase the surface area for ATP synthesis.
The smaller ribosome type found in prokaryotes, mitochondria and chloroplasts (made of 30S and 50S subunits).

workedExamples.q: A cell organelle is 2.5 μm long. Its image in a micrograph is 37.5 mm. Calculate the magnification.

mistakes: Confusing magnification (how large the image is) with resolution (how much detail can be seen).
Stating that ribosomes are 'found on the rough ER' — they are free in cytoplasm AND on RER.
Forgetting that prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes, not 80S.
tips: Always check units when calculating magnification — convert to the same unit first.
Link organelle to function: 'mitochondria have cristae to increase surface area for ATP synthase/electron transport chain.'
Learn which organelles are absent in prokaryotes: no nuclear envelope, no mitochondria, no Golgi, no ER.

flashcards.a: Magnification = image size / actual size (M = I/A). Convert to same units first.

flashcards.q: What is the function of the Golgi apparatus?
flashcards.a: Modifies, processes and packages proteins (and lipids) into vesicles for secretion or use within the cell.

flashcards.q: What type of ribosome do prokaryotes have?
What is the resolution of a transmission electron microscope?
flashcards.a: ~0.1 nm — much better than the light microscope (~200 nm).

flashcards.q: What is the function of lysosomes?
flashcards.a: Contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down waste materials, old organelles (autophagy), and pathogens.

flashcards.q: Name three features of a prokaryotic cell not found in eukaryotic cells.
flashcards.a: Circular DNA, plasmids, 70S ribosomes, peptidoglycan cell wall, flagellum (any 3).

questions.q: Which organelle is the site of the Krebs cycle?
questions.exp: The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix; oxidative phosphorylation occurs on the inner membrane (cristae).

questions.q: What is the resolution of a light microscope?
questions.exp: Light microscopes have a maximum resolution of about 200 nm due to the wavelength of visible light.

questions.q: Which of these is present in prokaryotic cells but NOT eukaryotic cells?
questions.exp: Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules found in prokaryotes; eukaryotes do not have them.

questions.q: A cell image is 60 mm; actual cell is 30 μm. What is the magnification?
What is the function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum?
questions.exp: The RER is studded with ribosomes and is the site of synthesis and initial processing of proteins destined for export or membrane insertion.

recall: Describe the structure and function of mitochondria.
Calculate magnification from image and actual sizes.
Explain why electron microscopes have greater resolution than light microscopes.
List organelles found in plant cells but not animal cells.
